320955.title: Local induced-cycle conjecture for vertex-prescribed deletion
320955.literal_statement:
A graph is **$r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves it connected. An induced cycle is a cycle with no edges between nonconsecutive cycle vertices.

**Vertex-prescribed induced-cycle conjecture.** For every $k$, there exists an $h(k)$ such that for every vertex $v$ of every $h(k)$-connected graph $G$, there exists an induced cycle $C$ containing $v$ such that $G-V(C)$ is $k$-connected.

This is a weaker local form of the high-connectivity-keeping cycle problem, while the corresponding edge-prescribed form is equivalent to the high-connectivity-keeping path conjecture. The source states that this problem is open.

376778.title: Absence of pure point spectrum under dynamical avoidance
376778.literal_statement:
Let $d_\infty$ and $N$ be the parameters in the spectral construction, let $\phi$ be the associated map, let $g$ be the associated rational map, and let $I_{g^n}$ denote the indeterminacy points of $g^n$. For every real $\lambda$, assume there are open subsets $U\subset\mathbb C$ and $V\subset\mathbb L^G$ such that

$$
\lambda\in U,\qquad \bigcup_{n=1}^{\infty} I_{g^n}\subset V,\qquad g^n(\phi(U))\cap V=\emptyset.
$$

**Pure point spectrum conjecture.** If $d_\infty=N$ and this condition holds for every real $\lambda$, then

$$
\Sigma_{pp}=\emptyset.
$$

The question arises because the non-deterministic spectrum is related to the indeterminacy points of $g$, while pure point spectrum beyond the non-deterministic component would suggest that iterates of $g$ approach those points. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

379937.title: Existence of sets with prescribed numbers of missing sums and differences

$$
|S+S|=2n-1-j,\qquad |S-S|=2n-1-k.
$$

This is posed as an open problem motivated by the preceding limiting-distribution conjecture. The source notes that Hegarty's methods establish it when $j\ge k/2$, while the general case remains open there.

351630.title: Weak-domination conjecture for reflective tree decompositions
351630.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected non-trivial bigraph, and let $T$ be a **reflective tree decomposition** of $G$ with core $H$. For each edge $\{U_1,U_2\}\in E(T)$, assume that $H$ weakly dominates $G\vert_{U_1\cap U_2}$. For every non-empty $V\subseteq V(T)$, **the weak-domination conjecture** asserts that $G$ weakly dominates

$$
G\vert_{\bigcup_{U\in V}U}.
$$

This is proposed as a natural generalization of a previously proved result on reflective tree decompositions and as a stepping stone toward replacing the forest restriction in higher-order decompositions by a weak-domination condition. The supplied text presents it as an open problem, and gives no resolution.

334042.title: Van Kampen obstruction criterion for simplicial maps of trees
334042.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a tree and let $\varphi:K\to\mathbb R^2$ be a simplicial map. The van Kampen obstruction $v(\varphi)$ is the mod-$2$ obstruction defined from intersections of images of disjoint simplices; for polygonal lines, its vanishing is equivalent to approximability by embeddings.

**Van Kampen obstruction conjecture.** The van Kampen obstruction vanishes if and only if $\varphi$ is approximable by embeddings.

The corresponding equivalence is known for polygonal lines and is false for closed polygonal lines, including the standard $3$-winding. The question for simplicial maps of arbitrary trees is attributed to R. Skopenkov and Skopenkov's cited source, and remains unresolved in the supplied text.

317034.title: Universality of the polymatroid quasi-symmetric invariant
317034.literal_statement:
Let $\operatorname{PolyMat}$ be the vector space of polymatroids, let $\operatorname{QSym}$ be the quasi-symmetric-function space, and let ${\mathcal G}:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to\operatorname{QSym}$ be the valuative invariant in the preceding theorem. A map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$ is **valuative** when it preserves every rational linear relation among polymatroid base polytopes. **Universality conjecture.** For every $\mathbb{Q}$-linear valuative map $f:\operatorname{PolyMat}\to V$, there should exist a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $\psi:\operatorname{QSym}\to V$ such that

$$
\psi\circ {\mathcal G}=f.
$$

This asks whether every valuative invariant factors through ${\mathcal G}$; the supplied text does not establish whether this universal property holds.

369524.title: The commutativity conjecture for excedance–antiexcedance elements
369524.literal_statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\mathbf{k}[S_n]$ be its group algebra. For a permutation $w\in S_n$, write $\operatorname{exc}w$ for the number of $i\in[n]$ such that $w(i)>i$, and $\operatorname{anxc}w$ for the number of $i\in[n]$ such that $w(i)<i$. For $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, define

$$
\mathbf{X}_{a,b}:=\sumnonlimits\limits_{\substack{w\in S_n;\\operatorname{exc}w=a;\\operatorname{anxc}w=b}}w\in\mathbf{k}[S_n].
$$

**Commutativity conjecture.** For fixed $n$, the elements $\mathbf{X}_{a,b}$ commute for all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$; equivalently,

$$
\mathbf{X}_{a,b}\mathbf{X}_{c,d}=\mathbf{X}_{c,d}\mathbf{X}_{a,b}
$$

for all $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{N}$. This is presented as an open problem concerning a family of combinatorially defined elements in the symmetric group algebra; the excerpt gives no evidence of a resolution.

357889.title: Ryser's conjecture on rainbow cycle packings

357906.title: Good qubit LDPC codes yield good quantum LDPC rotor codes
357906.literal_statement:
Let $\phi_\infty(\mathcal{S})$ be a good qubit LDPC code, meaning that it has constant rate and relative distance. Let $p^*$ denote the parameter governing the local-dimension bound, and suppose that

$$
p^*<2\pi.
$$

**Rotor-code conjecture.** Under these assumptions, $\phi_\infty(\mathcal{S})$ represents a good quantum LDPC rotor code.

This conjecture proposes that the construction preserves goodness when imported from qubit stabilizer codes to rotor systems, whose two Pauli axes have local dimensions modeled by $\mathbb{R}_{2\pi}^{+}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$. The paper gives the construction under the stated bound but does not provide a proof that the resulting rotor code is good.

358013.title: Heng's NMDS code conjecture for the extended trace code
358013.literal_statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let

$$
\mu_{q+1}=\{x\in \mathbb{F}_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\},\qquad D=\mu_{q+1}\setminus\{-1\},
$$

and let $\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q:\mathbb{F}_{q^2}\to\mathbb{F}_q$ be the trace map, $\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(x)=x+x^q$. For $b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ and $c\in\mathbb{F}_q$, define

$$
c(b,c)=\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(bx+b)+c)_{x\in D},-\operatorname{Tr}^{q^2}_q(b)\bigr),
$$

and set

$$
\widetilde{\overline{C_D}}=\{c(b,c):b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2},\ c\in\mathbb{F}_q\}.
$$

**Heng's conjecture.** If $q>2$, then $\widetilde{\overline{C_D}}$ is a $[q+1,3,q-2]_q$ NMDS code.
This conjecture concerns the remaining family of NMDS codes identified by Heng; proving it establishes the asserted parameters and the NMDS property for this extended trace construction.

**Perfect Martin sequence conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{P}(G_1\setminus v_1)=\mathcal{P}(G_2\setminus v_2)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G_1^{\bullet})=\operatorname{\mathsf{M}}(G_2^{\bullet}).
$$

358052.title: Azevedo–Shumyatsky conciseness conjecture for commutators of non-commutator words
358052.literal_statement:
Let $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ be non-commutator words in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. For a group word $v=v(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$, write $v(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ for the word obtained by substituting the $u_i$ into $v$. A word is **concise** if, in every group, finiteness of its set of values implies finiteness of its verbal subgroup.

$$
\gamma_r(u_1,\ldots,u_r)=[u_1,\ldots,u_r]
$$

is concise.

This conjecture generalizes known conciseness results for commutators involving non-commutator words; the paper's abstract states that it proves this generalized conjecture for lower central and derived words.

358204.title: Tomon’s shifting conjecture for $(r,t)$-maximal families

Let $\mathcal G\subset 2^{[n]}$ be an **$(r,t)$-maximal family**, meaning a family maximal with respect to the relevant $(r,t)$-intersection property, and let $\mathcal H$ be a shifted family obtained from $\mathcal G$ by shifting. For $i=0,1,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{r}\right\rfloor$, define

$$

$$

**Tomon’s conjecture.** If $\mathcal H\subset\mathcal F_i^t(r)$, then

$$
\mathcal G\cong\mathcal F_i^t(r).
$$

The conjecture would generalize the lemma used in the paper and is proposed as a route toward stability results for $r$-wise $t$-intersecting families.

358269.title: Arbitrarily deep failure of log-concavity for independence polynomials of trees
358269.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a tree, let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number, and write its independence polynomial as

$$
I(G;x)=\sum_{j=0}^{\alpha(G)}i_jx^j.
$$

Here, log-concavity at the $j$th coefficient means $i_j^2\geq i_{j-1}i_{j+1}$. **Arbitrarily deep failure conjecture.** Log-concavity may fail at the coefficient indexed by $\alpha(G)-k$ for arbitrarily chosen $k\in\{1,2,\ldots,\alpha(G)-1\}$. This is motivated by an explicit tree whose failure occurs at the $\alpha(G)-2$ coefficient; the supplied text does not state whether the proposed extension has been proved or disproved.

327713.title: Manoussakis's pancyclicity conjecture for digraphs
327713.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a strongly connected digraph on $n$ vertices. For vertices $x,y,z\in V(D)$, say that $x$ is **nonadjacent** to $y$ when neither arc between them is present. A digraph is **pancyclic** if it contains directed cycles of every length allowed by the conjecture.

**Manoussakis's conjecture.** If, for every triple $x,y,z\in V(D)$ with $x$ nonadjacent to $y$, the inequalities

$$
d(x)+d(y)+d^+(x)+d^-(z)\geq 3n+1
$$

when $xz\notin A(D)$, and

$$
d(x)+d(y)+d^+(z)+d^-(x)\geq 3n+1
$$

when $zx\notin A(D)$, hold, then $D$ is pancyclic.

This is a proposed pancyclic analogue of Manoussakis-type Hamiltonicity degree conditions. The supplied source does not report a resolution.

329224.title: The Janson–Sós conjecture on quasi-random properties from graph averages
329224.literal_statement:
Let $F \neq K_2$ be a non-empty graph with vertex set $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m \in (0,1)$ satisfy

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \leqslant 1.
$$

Write $\mathcal{P}(F,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ for the property defined by the corresponding average over products of disjoint vertex sets, and let $p \in (0,1]$. **Janson–Sós conjecture.** The property $\mathcal{P}(F,\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m)$ is a quasi-random property for every $p \in (0,1]$. This addresses the problem of determining when these properties are always quasi-random; before this work it was unknown even for the path on three vertices and was stated as an open problem by Janson and Sós. The exceptional known non-example is $\mathcal{P}(K_2,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2})$; the claim excludes it.

329273.title: Alon–Shpilka–Umans' sunflower conjecture over ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$

Vectors $v_1,v_2,v_3\in{\mathbb Z}_D^n$ form a **$3$-sunflower** if, in every coordinate, their entries are either all equal or all distinct. **Alon–Shpilka–Umans' sunflower conjecture.** There exist $\varepsilon>0$, $D_0$, and $n_0$ such that for every $D\geq D_0$ and $n\geq n_0$, every collection ${\cal F}$ of vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_D^n$ with

$$
|{\cal F}|\geq D^{(1-\varepsilon)n}
$$

contains a $3$-sunflower. This is an equivalent vector formulation of the Boolean-cube sunflower conjecture and is widely believed to be true, but remains open.

329466.title: Perrot–Pham sink-independence conjecture for the Biggs–Merino polynomial
329466.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph, and let $s$ be a sink vertex. For the set of $s$-recurrent configurations modulo the relation $\stackrel{s}{\sim}$, define the Biggs–Merino polynomial by

$$
\mathcal B(G,s;y):=\sum_{[\widehat{\mathbf{c}}]\in\operatorname{Rec}(G,\stackrel{s}{\sim})}y^{\operatorname{dlvl}([\widehat{\mathbf{c}}])}.
$$

**Perrot–Pham's conjecture.** The polynomial $\mathcal B(G,s;y)$ is independent of the choice of the sink vertex $s$.

Perrot and Pham proved this independence for connected Eulerian digraphs and conjectured it for all strongly connected digraphs. The paper states that its main theorem answers this conjecture, so the conjecture is solved.

331918.title: Ben Efraim's lexicographic edge-isoperimetric conjecture for the transposition graph
331918.literal_statement:

$$
|\partial \mathcal{A}| \geq |\partial \mathcal{C}|.
$$

This would give an edge-isoperimetric inequality for the transposition graph that is sharp for every set size; the source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
